title: Down and Up: The Phase of a Leg, How Long It Stands and Swings, and Where the Foot Should Come Down

artifact.note: the timing of a gait for four legs: a period, a duty factor (the fraction of the period each foot is on the ground) and a phase offset for each leg; the phase of a leg at a time, whether it is in stance or swing and how far through that part it is; how many feet are on the ground, for a walk (duty three quarters) and a trot (a half) and what a duty under a half does; the velocity of a stance foot in the body's frame (minus the body's velocity and its turn); and where to put the foot down (the foot's default place under the hip, moved ahead by half the distance the body travels in the stance, and by a correction that pushes against a speed that is too high)
